title: Integration of AI and Geophysical Sensing for Environmental Risk Assessment
abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) with geophysical sensing provides a scalable and data-driven solution for environmental risk assessment. This study presents a supervised machine learning framework designed to classify environmental risk levels (low, medium, and high) using statistical features extracted from simulated geophysical signals.
methodology: Synthetic geophysical signal simulation, statistical feature extraction using mean, standard deviation, and RMS, 70:30 stratified train-test split, optional SMOTE class balancing, and Random Forest classification.
dataset: 500 simulated geophysical signal samples with approximately balanced Low, Medium, and High risk classes.
findings: The Random Forest model achieved approximately 76% accuracy on the reported testing dataset. The paper also reports accuracy exceeding 85% in balanced scenarios and above 90% in optimized configurations using data balancing techniques.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Satellite-Based Infrastructure for Environmental Sustainability: Opportunities in the Context of Global Technology Ecosystems
abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI), satellite-based communication infrastructure, and renewable energy systems represents a critical technological pathway toward achieving long-term environmental sustainability. Advances in low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite networks, intelligent energy management systems, and AI-driven analytics have enabled new approaches to environmental monitoring, risk assessment, and sustainable resource optimization. This paper explores a conceptual and simulation-based framework for applying AI-enabled satellite infrastructure to environmental sustainability challenges in Indonesia.
methodology: A conceptual and simulation-based framework using MATLAB-generated synthetic environmental data and a supervised artificial neural network (ANN) model. The workflow includes synthetic data generation, data normalization, ANN training and validation, and performance evaluation using mean squared error (MSE).
dataset: Simulated environmental data generated using MATLAB, representing remote Indonesian environmental conditions. Variables include surface temperature variation, atmospheric CO2 concentration, energy consumption patterns, and renewable energy availability indicators.
findings: The ANN model effectively captures nonlinear relationships among environmental variables and achieves low prediction error in the simulation. The results indicate the feasibility and scalability of AI-driven environmental risk assessment using satellite-derived environmental indicators under simulated conditions.
